content_html:
A desktop coding agent for macOS and Linux. Any model, on your code and UI.

Download for macOS · Download for Linux · What's new

Harness Studio is a desktop app that works like Claude Code desktop, with whichever model provider you have an API key for. Download it, choose a model, open a project folder and ask.

What it does

  • Point at your UI, tell the agent what to change. Open your app's dev server in the Browser pane, pick an element, and say "make this bigger": the agent gets the element's source file and line, component, text, styles and HTML.
  • A browser the agent can use: it opens pages, reads them, clicks and types in the Browser pane, next to the conversation, with real mouse and keyboard input. In the desktop app it also reads what DevTools shows on your own development pages (localhost and your local network): console errors with stack traces, network requests with their status, and response bodies. It never attaches DevTools to public sites.
  • Documents, decks and spreadsheets: the agent writes PowerPoint, Word and Excel files, with editable charts in decks and spreadsheets, renders slides to check its own layout, and exports PDF, using a Python, Node and office converter bundled with the app, so nothing needs installing. Results open in the side pane's preview.
  • Design boards: ask the agent to design or mock up screens and it drafts them on one board, each screen and variant side by side at phone, tablet and desktop widths, using your project's own colours and fonts, before any app code changes. The board is a single HTML file with pan and zoom that opens in the preview pane or any browser.
  • Desktop and mobile apps: the agent builds Mac, Android and Linux desktop apps (and iPhone apps when Xcode is installed) inside its sandbox, keeping every tool's downloads in the project, then runs them and checks them: Mac apps through computer use, Android apps in a headless emulator with its screenshots, and web-based ones in the Browser pane.
  • Live dashboards: ask for a dashboard and the agent builds a page of charts with a small refresh script per data source (a spreadsheet, CSV, a database or warehouse through your own login, or a web API). The Dashboards pane fetches fresh data every time you open it, once you have approved the refresh scripts at their exact text; Keep fresh refreshes it while closed, and Save snapshot gives you one HTML file with today's data to send.
  • Charts, icons and diagrams: editable charts inside PowerPoint and Excel files, and SVG files for standalone charts, icon sets and flow or architecture diagrams, drawn from your data with nothing to install.
  • Speech to text, on this computer: the microphone button between the model picker and Send dictates into your message (a menu in the recording bar picks the language), and the agent can transcribe an audio or video file, or a part you marked in the Files tab, with the time each piece was said, in Chinese, English, Cantonese, Japanese or Korean. Recognition is Harness's local SenseVoice model (about 241 MB, downloaded once after you agree); no audio leaves the computer. When the agent needs ffmpeg and you have none, it asks once and downloads a pinned, checksum-checked build into Harness Studio's data folder.
  • Full-screen programs: the agent can run vim, less, top, interactive prompts and installers in a real terminal, read the screen and type into it, under the same sandbox as every other command.
  • Edit files yourself: press Edit on a file in the Files tab for a code editor with syntax colours and ⌘S; the agent's changes appear in place, and neither of you overwrites the other's unsaved work.
  • Side panes: Files, Changes, Session details, Browser and Terminal, stacked with a draggable divider.
  • Git history: a Git page in the sidebar shows every workspace's branch, upstream and uncommitted files, and each workspace's commits with a branch graph, search by message, author or changed code, every commit's files and diffs, and blame. Its Branch menu switches branches when nothing is uncommitted.
  • Connectors: add MCP servers by URL or command, with OAuth sign-in and per-session on/off.
  • Separate sessions: the agent can hand a piece of work to a new session in the sidebar with a written brief, optionally in its own git worktree, and gets that session's report back. For a self-contained job whose material is not needed afterwards, such as judging a batch of rendered frames, it uses a helper agent and keeps only the verdict.
  • Watches: the agent (or you, from the eye button in the session header) can watch a command's output, a port or files; the checks run on your computer without the model, and the agent is woken with a short notice only when something changes.
  • Remember: when you correct the agent or ask it to remember something, it proposes a one-line note; you approve it and choose this project or all your projects, and it's saved as a line in an instruction file you can edit.
  • Your own Chrome: an optional paired extension lets the agent browse in your real Chrome, where you are signed in, and lets you pick elements on any page with ⌥⇧S.
  • A calmer look: Claude Code–like density, text sizes, sidebar and zoom.
  • Secret files stay out of reach: commands the agent runs, and its file tools, cannot read your SSH keys, cloud and registry credentials, password files, .env files outside the project, or the app's own API keys, so a prompt injection in a README or web page cannot make the agent send them anywhere. What the agent can still send, and where, is spelled out in the app's About page under Safety model.
  • Command rules, like Claude Code's: block a tool call or ask first, for example never curl, ask before git push, never read ./.env, in Claude Code's permissions format, in ~/.harness-studio/permissions.json or a project's .harness-studio/permissions.json.
  • No account, no telemetry: there is no sign-in and no usage reporting, and your API keys are stored only on your machine and sent only to the provider they belong to.

Harness Studio is built on DeepSeek Harness, the open-source, any-model agent app. It is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek or Anthropic; their names are used only to describe compatibility and inspiration.

Screenshots

Files pane: the project's tree beside open files with line numbers and syntax colours. Type ? in the filter to search inside files.

Changes pane: the working tree against its branch, with per-file counts and coloured diffs.

The + menu: files, goals, plan mode, commands and per-session connectors in a compact popover above the message box.

Automation tasks: ask for a follow-up later, and the agent schedules it and replies in the same session when it fires.

Status

Developer preview, version 0.3.2, built on Harness 0.2.1-rc.2 through Harness Studio's fork of it, harness-studio-core (pinned in docs/HARNESS_PIN.md). Tested on macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux (x64 and arm64). Windows isn't available yet.

Planned, not yet built:

  • A full design canvas, like Claude Design: frames you drag and resize by hand, comments, and a design-system library. Until then, design boards (above) cover drafting and comparing screens; you change them by asking.
  • Image generation. The agent has no image model yet, so it can only draw graphics through code (SVG, HTML or the bundled Python image library).
  • Slide and document templates: a gallery of ready-made deck and document designs. For now the agent styles each file from scratch.
  • Video making, as a separate app. Animated videos and 3D product shots made as code (with Remotion) were tried in Harness Studio and taken out: rendering needs a 1 GB install and much of an 8 GB machine's memory. They are planned as their own app built from the same fork, so Harness Studio stays light. Video and audio files still play in Files and the preview, where you can mark a part for the agent.

Setup

1. Install Harness Studio

Harness Studio is a ready-to-run desktop app with the plugins built in, so you don't need DeepSeek Harness, Node.js or a build. Download it from the Releases page:

  • macOS (Apple Silicon): a .dmg; drag Harness Studio to Applications.
  • Linux (x64, arm64): an AppImage for most distributions, or a .deb for Debian and Ubuntu (sudo apt install ./harness-studio_<version>_amd64.deb).

Windows isn't available yet. How each app is built, and what to know before installing on Linux, is in desktop/README.md.

First launch on macOS

The Mac app isn't signed or notarised by Apple, so macOS blocks it the first time. Allow it once:

  1. Open the .dmg and drag Harness Studio to Applications.
  2. Open Harness Studio. macOS says it "cannot verify" the app; click Done (not Move to Trash).
  3. Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll to Security, and click Open Anyway next to the Harness Studio message.
  4. Confirm with Open Anyway and your password or Touch ID.

After that it opens normally. If macOS instead says the app "is damaged and can't be opened", the download's quarantine flag is the cause, not a broken file; clear it and open the app again:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Harness Studio.app"

To check the download first, compare shasum -a 256 Harness-Studio-<version>-mac-arm64.dmg with the .sha256 file published next to it.

2. Choose a model

On first launch, click Choose a model provider and add an API key for any provider in Settings → Models.

Chrome extension (optional): follow chrome-bridge/README.md to load the extension and add its connector, so the agent can use your own Chrome.

3. Optional: prepare your app for picking (development only)

The companion script and source loader come from this repository: git clone https://github.com/vigneshv1cky/harness-studio.git, then run the commands below from its folder.

a. Companion script — copy it into your app and load it only in development.

cp plugins/devpreview-companion/companion.js /path/to/your-app/public/devpreview-companion.js

Next.js App Router, in app/layout.tsx (inside <body>):

import Script from "next/script";

{process.env.NODE_ENV === "development" && (
  <Script src="/devpreview-companion.js" strategy="afterInteractive" />
)}

Plain HTML: <script src="/devpreview-companion.js"></script> in development pages only.

b. Source locations (Next.js 16 / Turbopack) — install the loader and add the rule.

npm install --save-dev /path/to/harness-studio/plugins/devpreview-source-loader
// next.config.ts
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  allowedDevOrigins: ["127.0.0.1"],          // only needed if you open the dev server as 127.0.0.1
  turbopack: {
    rules: {
      "*.{jsx,tsx}": {
        condition: { all: ["development", { not: "foreign" }] },
        loaders: [{ loader: "devpreview-source-loader", options: { root: process.cwd() } }],
        // no `as` — it would rename modules and break relative imports
      },
    },
  },
};

Without the loader, Pick still works; the agent locates the element from its text, selector and component names instead of an exact line.

4. Use it

  1. Start your dev server (npm run dev).
  2. In Harness Studio, set the Session's workspace to your app's folder (so the agent can edit without extra approvals and paths match the stamps).
  3. Click the Browser icon in the conversation header and open your dev server: type localhost:3000, or pick it from the Dev servers menu in the pane header.
  4. Click Pick (the arrow) in the bar at the bottom of the browser, hover, click an element. The card shows its source, text, size, selector and styles.
  5. Click Send to agent — a reference like [Selected <button> in CounterButton · src/app/counter-button.tsx:8:5] lands in the message box.
  6. Type what you want ("make this bigger", "use the brand blue", "move it under the heading") and send.
  7. ✕ on the card clears the selection for the agent.

Your instructions

Harness Studio follows instruction files the way Claude Code follows CLAUDE.md. It reads, in this order:

File Applies to
~/.harness-studio/AGENTS.md Every session: your personal rules for Harness Studio
~/.agents/AGENTS.md Every session: rules shared with other agent tools that read this folder
AGENTS.md, or CLAUDE.md when a folder has no AGENTS.md (and likewise AGENTS.local.md, else CLAUDE.local.md) in your project Sessions in that project, from the repository root down to the session's folder

Each folder contributes one file, so a repository that keeps both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md for different tools isn't charged twice. Files can include other files with an @path line, as in Claude Code; a line that includes an instruction file Harness Studio already reads, such as a CLAUDE.md containing just @AGENTS.md, is skipped. A project's files may only include files inside that project; your personal file may include any file, so to reuse your Claude Code rules put this line in ~/.harness-studio/AGENTS.md:

@~/.claude/CLAUDE.md

Instructions, in the left sidebar below Automation tasks, lists every file a workspace reads with its size, token cost and status, lets you edit or open each one, and sets the size limit. All instructions together may use up to 128 KB by default; the page offers 64 KB to 1 MB, or no limit. When they're larger, the broadest files are left out first and then the most specific one is shortened, and the instructions row at the start of the conversation names each file left out or cut, with its size. Editing an included file takes effect in the next session.

Command line

From 0.3.0, Harness Studio includes a harness-studio command for scripts, CI and one-off jobs. On macOS, choose Install Command-Line Tool… in the app menu, below Check for Updates…; it adds /usr/local/bin/harness-studio and may ask for your password. On Linux, the .deb installs it as /usr/bin/harness-studio (open the app itself from your applications menu); the AppImage does not include the command. Open a new terminal and check it:

harness-studio --version

Give it a task, and it runs one agent session in the current folder with the same model, tools, sandbox, network setting, connectors, memory and hooks as the app, prints the final answer and exits (exit code 0 when the task finished, 1 when it failed):

harness-studio "run the tests and fix any failures"

With no task argument it reads the task from standard input, so you can pipe text in:

tail -n 100 error.log | harness-studio
git diff origin/main | harness-studio

Put the whole prompt in the pipe in that case (for example { echo "Review this diff for security risks:"; git diff origin/main; } | harness-studio); a task argument and piped input are not combined.

Run it with no task in a terminal to chat: each line you type is one message in the same session, and the answer prints below it. Ctrl-C stops the reply in progress (or quits at the prompt), Ctrl-D or /exit quits, and the session id it prints at the end continues the conversation later with --session-id.

harness-studio

Other options:

Option Does
--json Print a stream of JSON events (one per line) instead of plain text, for scripts
--session-id <id> Continue an existing session instead of starting a new one
--help List the options

The command uses the app's home folder (~/.harness-studio), so it shares your saved model key, settings, connectors and memory. It cannot ask you questions: approval cards are refused, and a project's hooks run only if you already allowed them in the app. Install the app in Applications first; remove the command from the same menu before uninstalling the app.

Privacy and safety

  • The companion and loader only run in development; keep them out of production builds.
  • The companion obeys only the Harness browser pane that shows it (Web: parent window, verified origin; Desktop: the pane's own embedded browser).
  • Element details go to your configured model provider as part of the conversation. Don't pick elements showing secrets.
  • The Harness Studio app has product analytics and session telemetry off, and no Session-log upload. If you add the plugins to your own Harness instead, consider DSH_TELEMETRY_MODE=DISABLED, and turn off Upload Session Log when using the official model API in Settings → General.
  • The Browser pane in Harness Studio is a separate browser from your own; the optional Chrome extension is what lets the agent use your real Chrome, and only after you pair it.
  • A web address can carry anything the agent has read, so web fetch, Browser pane pages and pages in your Chrome ask before reaching a site for the first time in a session (sites on this computer, and those on the Network for commands list while it is set to Only allowed sites, pass). Connectors don't ask by default; set Ask before calls on one that can send things where others read them. The About page's Safety model section lists what each guard covers and what it leaves open.

Troubleshooting

Symptom Cause and fix
"No companion script on this page" The page doesn't load devpreview-companion.js, or (Next.js) the page never hydrated — opening the dev server as 127.0.0.1 without allowedDevOrigins. Use localhost or add the origin.
Source says "not stamped" The loader isn't running: check the turbopack.rules entry, run npm install inside the loader folder if it was installed as a link, and restart next dev after deleting .next.
Can't resolve './x.tsx.tsx' Remove as from the loader rule.
Preview doesn't show the agent's change Pages without hot reload need the browser's reload button. Next.js updates on its own.
Desktop: plugin can't be installed from the CLI The Desktop profile is managed by the app — use Plugins → Add plugin.
Agent asks for approval to write The file is outside the Session's workspace; set the workspace to your app's folder.

Using the plugins with your own Harness

Only needed if you run DeepSeek Harness itself instead of the Harness Studio app.

Requirements:

  • Harness >=0.2.1-alpha.3 <0.3.0 (Desktop app, or dsh from source — see Running the Harness from source).
  • A model configured in Harness (any provider it supports).
  • Node.js 24 for building from source (.nvmrc).

Get Harness Studio:

git clone https://github.com/vigneshv1cky/harness-studio.git
cd harness-studio

Build the installable files:

npm pack --pack-destination dist ./plugins/devpreview ./plugins/connectors ./plugins/compact

Harness Desktop: Plugins → Add plugin → enter the absolute path of each .tgz in dist/ → Install → Enable now. compact (the look) is optional.

Browser pane sign-in: the desktop app has it as a setting (app menu → Allow Sign-in in Browser Pane); see desktop/README.md.

Web / CLI:

dsh plugin --profile web add ./dist/harness-studio-devpreview-0.1.0.tgz

For plugin development, install the folder as a link instead so edits apply on reload: dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/plugins/devpreview (Desktop: enter the folder path in Add plugin).

Running the Harness from source

git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git harness
git -C harness checkout 571902028a75c64c1d767f4ae5fd099485f0ddf0
cd harness
nvm use 24
pnpm install
pnpm run build                 # ~5 minutes
pnpm --filter @deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop exec install-electron
pnpm run start:desktop         # Desktop app, or:
pnpm dsh web                   # Web app on http://127.0.0.1:3080

Development

  • The plugin, companion and loader are plain JavaScript with no build step.
  • The Desktop tab carries a copy of the companion so it can add the picker to live websites. After editing plugins/devpreview-companion/companion.js, run node scripts/embed-companion.mjs (or --check to verify it is in sync).
  • Sample apps: python3 examples/hello-app/serve.py (port 3000, no-cache) and cd examples/next-app && npm install && npx next dev -p 3001.
  • A separate Harness home for testing keeps your real setup untouched: DSH_HOME=$PWD/.dsh-home dsh plugin --profile web add link:$PWD/plugins/devpreview, then DSH_HOME=$PWD/.dsh-home dsh web.

Type ? in the filter to search inside files. Changes pane: the working tree against its branch, with per-file counts and coloured diffs. Separate sessions: the agent proposes handing a task to a new session with its own git worktree, and you start it or keep the work in this session. Connectors: MCP servers such as GitHub and the Chrome extension, each with its status and tool count, added by URL or command. The + menu: files, goals, plan mode, commands and per-session connectors in a compact popover above the message box. Session pane: the session's changes and its usage at a glance. Automation tasks: ask for a follow-up later, and the agent schedules it and replies in the same session when it fires. Status Developer preview, version 0.3.2, built on Harness 0.2.1-rc.2 through Harness Studio's fork of it, harness-studio-core (pinned in docs/HARNESS_PIN.md). Tested on macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux (x64 and arm64). Windows isn't available yet. Planned, not yet built: A full design canvas, like Claude Design: frames you drag and resize by hand, comments, and a design-system library. Until then, design boards (above) cover drafting and comparing screens; you change them by asking. Image generation. The agent has no image model yet, so it can only draw graphics through code (SVG, HTML or the bundled Python image library). Slide and document templates: a gallery of ready-made deck and document designs. For now the agent styles each file from scratch. Video making, as a separate app. Animated videos and 3D product shots made as code (with Remotion) were tried in Harness Studio and taken out: rendering needs a 1 GB install and much of an 8 GB machine's memory. They are planned as their own app built from the same fork, so Harness Studio stays light. Video and audio files still play in Files and the preview, where you can mark a part for the agent. Setup 1. Install Harness Studio Harness Studio is a ready-to-run desktop app with the plugins built in, so you don't need DeepSeek Harness, Node.js or a build. Download it from the Releases page: macOS (Apple Silicon): a .dmg; drag Harness Studio to Applications. Linux (x64, arm64): an AppImage for most distributions, or a .deb for Debian and Ubuntu (sudo apt install ./harness-studio_<version>_amd64.deb). Windows isn't available yet. How each app is built, and what to know before installing on Linux, is in desktop/README.md. First launch on macOS The Mac app isn't signed or notarised by Apple, so macOS blocks it the first time. Allow it once: Open the .dmg and drag Harness Studio to Applications. Open Harness Studio. macOS says it "cannot verify" the app; click Done (not Move to Trash). Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll to Security, and click Open Anyway next to the Harness Studio message. Confirm with Open Anyway and your password or Touch ID. After that it opens normally. If macOS instead says the app "is damaged and can't be opened", the download's quarantine flag is the cause, not a broken file; clear it and open the app again: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Harness Studio.app" To check the download first, compare shasum -a 256 Harness-Studio-<version>-mac-arm64.dmg with the .sha256 file published next to it. 2. Choose a model On first launch, click Choose a model provider and add an API key for any provider in Settings → Models. Chrome extension (optional): follow chrome-bridge/README.md to load the extension and add its connector, so the agent can use your own Chrome. 3. Optional: prepare your app for picking (development only) The companion script and source loader come from this repository: git clone https://github.com/vigneshv1cky/harness-studio.git, then run the commands below from its folder. a. Companion script — copy it into your app and load it only in development. cp plugins/devpreview-companion/companion.js /path/to/your-app/public/devpreview-companion.js Next.js App Router, in app/layout.tsx (inside <body>): import Script from "next/script"; {process.env.NODE_ENV === "development" && ( <Script src="/devpreview-companion.js" strategy="afterInteractive" /> )} Plain HTML: <script src="/devpreview-companion.js"></script> in development pages only. b. Source locations (Next.js 16 / Turbopack) — install the loader and add the rule. npm install --save-dev /path/to/harness-studio/plugins/devpreview-source-loader // next.config.ts const nextConfig: NextConfig = { allowedDevOrigins: ["127.0.0.1"], // only needed if you open the dev server as 127.0.0.1 turbopack: { rules: { "*.{jsx,tsx}": { condition: { all: ["development", { not: "foreign" }] }, loaders: [{ loader: "devpreview-source-loader", options: { root: process.cwd() } }], // no `as` — it would rename modules and break relative imports }, }, }, }; Without the loader, Pick still works; the agent locates the element from its text, selector and component names instead of an exact line. 4. Use it Start your dev server (npm run dev). In Harness Studio, set the Session's workspace to your app's folder (so the agent can edit without extra approvals and paths match the stamps). Click the Browser icon in the conversation header and open your dev server: type localhost:3000, or pick it from the Dev servers menu in the pane header. Click Pick (the arrow) in the bar at the bottom of the browser, hover, click an element. The card shows its source, text, size, selector and styles. Click Send to agent — a reference like [Selected <button> in CounterButton · src/app/counter-button.tsx:8:5] lands in the message box. Type what you want ("make this bigger", "use the brand blue", "move it under the heading") and send. ✕ on the card clears the selection for the agent. Your instructions Harness Studio follows instruction files the way Claude Code follows CLAUDE.md. It reads, in this order: File Applies to ~/.harness-studio/AGENTS.md Every session: your personal rules for Harness Studio ~/.agents/AGENTS.md Every session: rules shared with other agent tools that read this folder AGENTS.md, or CLAUDE.md when a folder has no AGENTS.md (and likewise AGENTS.local.md, else CLAUDE.local.md) in your project Sessions in that project, from the repository root down to the session's folder Each folder contributes one file, so a repository that keeps both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md for different tools isn't charged twice. Files can include other files with an @path line, as in Claude Code; a line that includes an instruction file Harness Studio already reads, such as a CLAUDE.md containing just @AGENTS.md, is skipped. A project's files may only include files inside that project; your personal file may include any file, so to reuse your Claude Code rules put this line in ~/.harness-studio/AGENTS.md: @~/.claude/CLAUDE.md Instructions, in the left sidebar below Automation tasks, lists every file a workspace reads with its size, token cost and status, lets you edit or open each one, and sets the size limit. All instructions together may use up to 128 KB by default; the page offers 64 KB to 1 MB, or no limit. When they're larger, the broadest files are left out first and then the most specific one is shortened, and the instructions row at the start of the conversation names each file left out or cut, with its size. Editing an included file takes effect in the next session. Command line From 0.3.0, Harness Studio includes a harness-studio command for scripts, CI and one-off jobs. On macOS, choose Install Command-Line Tool… in the app menu, below Check for Updates…; it adds /usr/local/bin/harness-studio and may ask for your password. On Linux, the .deb installs it as /usr/bin/harness-studio (open the app itself from your applications menu); the AppImage does not include the command. Open a new terminal and check it: harness-studio --version Give it a task, and it runs one agent session in the current folder with the same model, tools, sandbox, network setting, connectors, memory and hooks as the app, prints the final answer and exits (exit code 0 when the task finished, 1 when it failed): harness-studio "run the tests and fix any failures" With no task argument it reads the task from standard input, so you can pipe text in: tail -n 100 error.log | harness-studio git diff origin/main | harness-studio Put the whole prompt in the pipe in that case (for example { echo "Review this diff for security risks:"; git diff origin/main; } | harness-studio); a task argument and piped input are not combined. Run it with no task in a terminal to chat: each line you type is one message in the same session, and the answer prints below it. Ctrl-C stops the reply in progress (or quits at the prompt), Ctrl-D or /exit quits, and the session id it prints at the end continues the conversation later with --session-id. harness-studio Other options: Option Does --json Print a stream of JSON events (one per line) instead of plain text, for scripts --session-id <id> Continue an existing session instead of starting a new one --help List the options The command uses the app's home folder (~/.harness-studio), so it shares your saved model key, settings, connectors and memory. It cannot ask you questions: approval cards are refused, and a project's hooks run only if you already allowed them in the app. Install the app in Applications first; remove the command from the same menu before uninstalling the app. Privacy and safety The companion and loader only run in development; keep them out of production builds. The companion obeys only the Harness browser pane that shows it (Web: parent window, verified origin; Desktop: the pane's own embedded browser). Element details go to your configured model provider as part of the conversation. Don't pick elements showing secrets. The Harness Studio app has product analytics and session telemetry off, and no Session-log upload. If you add the plugins to your own Harness instead, consider DSH_TELEMETRY_MODE=DISABLED, and turn off Upload Session Log when using the official model API in Settings → General. The Browser pane in Harness Studio is a separate browser from your own; the optional Chrome extension is what lets the agent use your real Chrome, and only after you pair it. A web address can carry anything the agent has read, so web fetch, Browser pane pages and pages in your Chrome ask before reaching a site for the first time in a session (sites on this computer, and those on the Network for commands list while it is set to Only allowed sites, pass). Connectors don't ask by default; set Ask before calls on one that can send things where others read them. The About page's Safety model section lists what each guard covers and what it leaves open. Troubleshooting Symptom Cause and fix "No companion script on this page" The page doesn't load devpreview-companion.js, or (Next.js) the page never hydrated — opening the dev server as 127.0.0.1 without allowedDevOrigins. Use localhost or add the origin. Source says "not stamped" The loader isn't running: check the turbopack.rules entry, run npm install inside the loader folder if it was installed as a link, and restart next dev after deleting .next. Can't resolve './x.tsx.tsx' Remove as from the loader rule. Preview doesn't show the agent's change Pages without hot reload need the browser's reload button. Next.js updates on its own. Desktop: plugin can't be installed from the CLI The Desktop profile is managed by the app — use Plugins → Add plugin. Agent asks for approval to write The file is outside the Session's workspace; set the workspace to your app's folder. For developers Harness Studio's features are plugins and patches on top of Harness. This repository holds them, the scripts that build the app, and a Chrome extension. content_html_zh:
A desktop coding agent for macOS and Linux. Any model, on your code and UI.

Download for macOS · Download for Linux · What's new

Harness Studio is a desktop app that works like Claude Code desktop, with whichever model provider you have an API key for. Download it, choose a model, open a project folder and ask.

它的作用

  • Point at your UI, tell the agent what to change. Open your app's dev server in the Browser pane, pick an element, and say "make this bigger": the agent gets the element's source file and line, component, text, styles and HTML.
  • A browser the agent can use: it opens pages, reads them, clicks and types in the Browser pane, next to the conversation, with real mouse and keyboard input. In the desktop app it also reads what DevTools shows on your own development pages (localhost and your local network): console errors with stack traces, network requests with their status, and response bodies. It never attaches DevTools to public sites.
  • Documents, decks and spreadsheets: the agent writes PowerPoint, Word and Excel files, with editable charts in decks and spreadsheets, renders slides to check its own layout, and exports PDF, using a Python, Node and office converter bundled with the app, so nothing needs installing. Results open in the side pane's preview.
  • Design boards: ask the agent to design or mock up screens and it drafts them on one board, each screen and variant side by side at phone, tablet and desktop widths, using your project's own colours and fonts, before any app code changes. The board is a single HTML file with pan and zoom that opens in the preview pane or any browser.
  • Desktop and mobile apps: the agent builds Mac, Android and Linux desktop apps (and iPhone apps when Xcode is installed) inside its sandbox, keeping every tool's downloads in the project, then runs them and checks them: Mac apps through computer use, Android apps in a headless emulator with its screenshots, and web-based ones in the Browser pane.
  • Live dashboards: ask for a dashboard and the agent builds a page of charts with a small refresh script per data source (a spreadsheet, CSV, a database or warehouse through your own login, or a web API). The Dashboards pane fetches fresh data every time you open it, once you have approved the refresh scripts at their exact text; Keep fresh refreshes it while closed, and Save snapshot gives you one HTML file with today's data to send.
  • Charts, icons and diagrams: editable charts inside PowerPoint and Excel files, and SVG files for standalone charts, icon sets and flow or architecture diagrams, drawn from your data with nothing to install.
  • Speech to text, on this computer: the microphone button between the model picker and Send dictates into your message (a menu in the recording bar picks the language), and the agent can transcribe an audio or video file, or a part you marked in the Files tab, with the time each piece was said, in Chinese, English, Cantonese, Japanese or Korean. Recognition is Harness's local SenseVoice model (about 241 MB, downloaded once after you agree); no audio leaves the computer. When the agent needs ffmpeg and you have none, it asks once and downloads a pinned, checksum-checked build into Harness Studio's data folder.
  • Full-screen programs: the agent can run vim, less, top, interactive prompts and installers in a real terminal, read the screen and type into it, under the same sandbox as every other command.
  • Edit files yourself: press Edit on a file in the Files tab for a code editor with syntax colours and ⌘S; the agent's changes appear in place, and neither of you overwrites the other's unsaved work.
  • Side panes: Files, Changes, Session details, Browser and Terminal, stacked with a draggable divider.
  • Git history: a Git page in the sidebar shows every workspace's branch, upstream and uncommitted files, and each workspace's commits with a branch graph, search by message, author or changed code, every commit's files and diffs, and blame. Its Branch menu switches branches when nothing is uncommitted.
  • Connectors: add MCP servers by URL or command, with OAuth sign-in and per-session on/off.
  • Separate sessions: the agent can hand a piece of work to a new session in the sidebar with a written brief, optionally in its own git worktree, and gets that session's report back. For a self-contained job whose material is not needed afterwards, such as judging a batch of rendered frames, it uses a helper agent and keeps only the verdict.
  • Watches: the agent (or you, from the eye button in the session header) can watch a command's output, a port or files; the checks run on your computer without the model, and the agent is woken with a short notice only when something changes.
  • Remember: when you correct the agent or ask it to remember something, it proposes a one-line note; you approve it and choose this project or all your projects, and it's saved as a line in an instruction file you can edit.
  • Your own Chrome: an optional paired extension lets the agent browse in your real Chrome, where you are signed in, and lets you pick elements on any page with ⌥⇧S.
  • A calmer look: Claude Code–like density, text sizes, sidebar and zoom.
  • Secret files stay out of reach: commands the agent runs, and its file tools, cannot read your SSH keys, cloud and registry credentials, password files, .env files outside the project, or the app's own API keys, so a prompt injection in a README or web page cannot make the agent send them anywhere. What the agent can still send, and where, is spelled out in the app's About page under Safety model.
  • Command rules, like Claude Code's: block a tool call or ask first, for example never curl, ask before git push, never read ./.env, in Claude Code's permissions format, in ~/.harness-studio/permissions.json or a project's .harness-studio/permissions.json.
  • No account, no telemetry: there is no sign-in and no usage reporting, and your API keys are stored only on your machine and sent only to the provider they belong to.

Harness Studio is built on DeepSeek Harness, the open-source, any-model agent app. It is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek or Anthropic; their names are used only to describe compatibility and inspiration.

截图

Dark mode, with a reply that cites files and code from the project:

Files pane: the project's tree beside open files with line numbers and syntax colours. Type ? in the filter to search inside files.

Changes pane: the working tree against its branch, with per-file counts and coloured diffs.

Separate sessions: the agent proposes handing a task to a new session with its own git worktree, and you start it or keep the work in this session.

Connectors: MCP servers such as GitHub and the Chrome extension, each with its status and tool count, added by URL or command.

The + menu: files, goals, plan mode, commands and per-session connectors in a compact popover above the message box.

Session pane: the session's changes and its usage at a glance.

Automation tasks: ask for a follow-up later, and the agent schedules it and replies in the same session when it fires.

地位

Developer preview, version 0.3.2, built on Harness 0.2.1-rc.2 through Harness Studio's fork of it, harness-studio-core (pinned in docs/HARNESS_PIN.md). Tested on macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux (x64 and arm64). Windows isn't available yet.

Planned, not yet built:

  • A full design canvas, like Claude Design: frames you drag and resize by hand, comments, and a design-system library. Until then, design boards (above) cover drafting and comparing screens; you change them by asking.
  • Image generation. The agent has no image model yet, so it can only draw graphics through code (SVG, HTML or the bundled Python image library).
  • Slide and document templates: a gallery of ready-made deck and document designs. For now the agent styles each file from scratch.
  • Video making, as a separate app. Animated videos and 3D product shots made as code (with Remotion) were tried in Harness Studio and taken out: rendering needs a 1 GB install and much of an 8 GB machine's memory. They are planned as their own app built from the same fork, so Harness Studio stays light. Video and audio files still play in Files and the preview, where you can mark a part for the agent.

Setup

1. Install Harness Studio

Harness Studio is a ready-to-run desktop app with the plugins built in, so you don't need DeepSeek Harness, Node.js or a build. Download it from the Releases page:

  • macOS (Apple Silicon): a .dmg; drag Harness Studio to Applications.
  • Linux (x64, arm64): an AppImage for most distributions, or a .deb for Debian and Ubuntu (sudo apt install ./harness-studio_<version>_amd64.deb).

Windows isn't available yet. How each app is built, and what to know before installing on Linux, is in desktop/README.md.

First launch on macOS

The Mac app isn't signed or notarised by Apple, so macOS blocks it the first time. Allow it once:

  1. Open the .dmg and drag Harness Studio to Applications.
  2. Open Harness Studio. macOS says it "cannot verify" the app; click Done (not Move to Trash).
  3. Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll to Security, and click Open Anyway next to the Harness Studio message.
  4. Confirm with Open Anyway and your password or Touch ID.

After that it opens normally. If macOS instead says the app "is damaged and can't be opened", the download's quarantine flag is the cause, not a broken file; clear it and open the app again:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Harness Studio.app"

To check the download first, compare shasum -a 256 Harness-Studio-<version>-mac-arm64.dmg with the .sha256 file published next to it.

2. 选择型号

On first launch, click Choose a model provider and add an API key for any provider in Settings → Models.

Chrome extension (optional): follow chrome-bridge/README.md to load the extension and add its connector, so the agent can use your own Chrome.

3. Optional: prepare your app for picking (development only)

The companion script and source loader come from this repository: git clone https://github.com/vigneshv1cky/harness-studio.git, then run the commands below from its folder.

一个。 Companion script — copy it into your app and load it only in development.

cp plugins/devpreview-companion/companion.js /path/to/your-app/public/devpreview-companion.js

Next.js App Router, in app/layout.tsx (inside <body>):

import Script from "next/script";

{process.env.NODE_ENV === "development" && (
  <Script src="/devpreview-companion.js" strategy="afterInteractive" />
)}

Plain HTML: <script src="/devpreview-companion.js"></script> in development pages only.

b. Source locations (Next.js 16 / Turbopack) — install the loader and add the rule.

npm install --save-dev /path/to/harness-studio/plugins/devpreview-source-loader
// next.config.ts
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  allowedDevOrigins: ["127.0.0.1"],          // only needed if you open the dev server as 127.0.0.1
  turbopack: {
    rules: {
      "*.{jsx,tsx}": {
        condition: { all: ["development", { not: "foreign" }] },
        loaders: [{ loader: "devpreview-source-loader", options: { root: process.cwd() } }],
        // no `as` — it would rename modules and break relative imports
      },
    },
  },
};

Without the loader, Pick still works; the agent locates the element from its text, selector and component names instead of an exact line.

4. Use it

  1. Start your dev server (npm run dev).
  2. In Harness Studio, set the Session's workspace to your app's folder (so the agent can edit without extra approvals and paths match the stamps).
  3. Click the Browser icon in the conversation header and open your dev server: type localhost:3000, or pick it from the Dev servers menu in the pane header.
  4. Click Pick (the arrow) in the bar at the bottom of the browser, hover, click an element. The card shows its source, text, size, selector and styles.
  5. Click Send to agent — a reference like [Selected <button> in CounterButton · src/app/counter-button.tsx:8:5] lands in the message box.
  6. Type what you want ("make this bigger", "use the brand blue", "move it under the heading") and send.
  7. ✕ on the card clears the selection for the agent.

Your instructions

Harness Studio follows instruction files the way Claude Code follows CLAUDE.md. It reads, in this order:

File 适用于
~/.harness-studio/AGENTS.md Every session: your personal rules for Harness Studio
~/.agents/AGENTS.md Every session: rules shared with other agent tools that read this folder
AGENTS.md, or CLAUDE.md when a folder has no AGENTS.md (and likewise AGENTS.local.md, else CLAUDE.local.md) in your project Sessions in that project, from the repository root down to the session's folder

Each folder contributes one file, so a repository that keeps both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md for different tools isn't charged twice. Files can include other files with an @path line, as in Claude Code; a line that includes an instruction file Harness Studio already reads, such as a CLAUDE.md containing just @AGENTS.md, is skipped. A project's files may only include files inside that project; your personal file may include any file, so to reuse your Claude Code rules put this line in ~/.harness-studio/AGENTS.md:

@~/.claude/CLAUDE.md

Instructions, in the left sidebar below Automation tasks, lists every file a workspace reads with its size, token cost and status, lets you edit or open each one, and sets the size limit. All instructions together may use up to 128 KB by default; the page offers 64 KB to 1 MB, or no limit. When they're larger, the broadest files are left out first and then the most specific one is shortened, and the instructions row at the start of the conversation names each file left out or cut, with its size. Editing an included file takes effect in the next session.

命令行

From 0.3.0, Harness Studio includes a harness-studio command for scripts, CI and one-off jobs. On macOS, choose Install Command-Line Tool… in the app menu, below Check for Updates…; it adds /usr/local/bin/harness-studio and may ask for your password. On Linux, the .deb installs it as /usr/bin/harness-studio (open the app itself from your applications menu); the AppImage does not include the command. Open a new terminal and check it:

harness-studio --version

Give it a task, and it runs one agent session in the current folder with the same model, tools, sandbox, network setting, connectors, memory and hooks as the app, prints the final answer and exits (exit code 0 when the task finished, 1 when it failed):

harness-studio "run the tests and fix any failures"

With no task argument it reads the task from standard input, so you can pipe text in:

tail -n 100 error.log | harness-studio
git diff origin/main | harness-studio

Put the whole prompt in the pipe in that case (for example { echo "Review this diff for security risks:"; git diff origin/main; } | harness-studio); a task argument and piped input are not combined.

Run it with no task in a terminal to chat: each line you type is one message in the same session, and the answer prints below it. Ctrl-C stops the reply in progress (or quits at the prompt), Ctrl-D or /exit quits, and the session id it prints at the end continues the conversation later with --session-id.

harness-studio

Other options:

选项 Does
--json Print a stream of JSON events (one per line) instead of plain text, for scripts
--session-id <id> Continue an existing session instead of starting a new one
--help List the options

The command uses the app's home folder (~/.harness-studio), so it shares your saved model key, settings, connectors and memory. It cannot ask you questions: approval cards are refused, and a project's hooks run only if you already allowed them in the app. Install the app in Applications first; remove the command from the same menu before uninstalling the app.

Privacy and safety

  • The companion and loader only run in development; keep them out of production builds.
  • The companion obeys only the Harness browser pane that shows it (Web: parent window, verified origin; Desktop: the pane's own embedded browser).
  • Element details go to your configured model provider as part of the conversation. Don't pick elements showing secrets.
  • The Harness Studio app has product analytics and session telemetry off, and no Session-log upload. If you add the plugins to your own Harness instead, consider DSH_TELEMETRY_MODE=DISABLED, and turn off Upload Session Log when using the official model API in Settings → General.
  • The Browser pane in Harness Studio is a separate browser from your own; the optional Chrome extension is what lets the agent use your real Chrome, and only after you pair it.
  • A web address can carry anything the agent has read, so web fetch, Browser pane pages and pages in your Chrome ask before reaching a site for the first time in a session (sites on this computer, and those on the Network for commands list while it is set to Only allowed sites, pass). Connectors don't ask by default; set Ask before calls on one that can send things where others read them. The About page's Safety model section lists what each guard covers and what it leaves open.

故障排除

症状 Cause and fix
"No companion script on this page" The page doesn't load devpreview-companion.js, or (Next.js) the page never hydrated — opening the dev server as 127.0.0.1 without allowedDevOrigins. Use localhost or add the origin.
Source says "not stamped" The loader isn't running: check the turbopack.rules entry, run npm install inside the loader folder if it was installed as a link, and restart next dev after deleting .next.
Can't resolve './x.tsx.tsx' Remove as from the loader rule.
Preview doesn't show the agent's change Pages without hot reload need the browser's reload button. Next.js updates on its own.
Desktop: plugin can't be installed from the CLI The Desktop profile is managed by the app — use Plugins → Add plugin.
Agent asks for approval to write The file is outside the Session's workspace; set the workspace to your app's folder.

Using the plugins with your own Harness

Only needed if you run DeepSeek Harness itself instead of the Harness Studio app.

要求：

  • Harness >=0.2.1-alpha.3 <0.3.0 (Desktop app, or dsh from source — see Running the Harness from source).
  • A model configured in Harness (any provider it supports).
  • Node.js 24 for building from source (.nvmrc).

Get Harness Studio:

git clone https://github.com/vigneshv1cky/harness-studio.git
cd harness-studio

Build the installable files:

npm pack --pack-destination dist ./plugins/devpreview ./plugins/connectors ./plugins/compact

Harness Desktop: Plugins → Add plugin → enter the absolute path of each .tgz in dist/ → Install → Enable now. compact (the look) is optional.

Browser pane sign-in: the desktop app has it as a setting (app menu → Allow Sign-in in Browser Pane); see desktop/README.md.

Web / CLI:

dsh plugin --profile web add ./dist/harness-studio-devpreview-0.1.0.tgz

For plugin development, install the folder as a link instead so edits apply on reload: dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/plugins/devpreview (Desktop: enter the folder path in Add plugin).

Running the Harness from source

git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git harness
git -C harness checkout 571902028a75c64c1d767f4ae5fd099485f0ddf0
cd harness
nvm use 24
pnpm install
pnpm run build                 # ~5 minutes
pnpm --filter @deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop exec install-electron
pnpm run start:desktop         # Desktop app, or:
pnpm dsh web                   # Web app on http://127.0.0.1:3080

发展

  • The plugin, companion and loader are plain JavaScript with no build step.
  • The Desktop tab carries a copy of the companion so it can add the picker to live websites. After editing plugins/devpreview-companion/companion.js, run node scripts/embed-companion.mjs (or --check to verify it is in sync).
  • Sample apps: python3 examples/hello-app/serve.py (port 3000, no-cache) and cd examples/next-app && npm install && npx next dev -p 3001.
  • A separate Harness home for testing keeps your real setup untouched: DSH_HOME=$PWD/.dsh-home dsh plugin --profile web add link:$PWD/plugins/devpreview, then DSH_HOME=$PWD/.dsh-home dsh web.
